name: Suzano Imperatriz Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 1,740 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp (expanded from 1,500 kt); Imperatriz, Maranhão
operator: Suzano S.A.
source: Valmet Suzano Imperatriz reference 'sets new standards for green energy'; Suzano investor relations; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,740 kt
notes: Imperatriz, Maranhão. One of Suzano's larger mills in northeast Brazil. Produces green energy surplus. No BECCS/CCS plans. Brazil's interior saline aquifer CO2 storage geology is limited — transport to coast required for offshore sequestration.

name: Suzano Mucuri Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~1,000 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp; Mucuri, southern Bahia
operator: Suzano S.A.
source: Environmental Paper Network Brazil pulp expansion report 2017; Suzano investor relations; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,000 kt
notes: Mucuri, Bahia coast. Coastal location offers slightly better CO2 transport potential than inland mills. No CCS plans. Produces significant bioelectricity from bark/black liquor. Part of Suzano's earliest operations.

name: Suzano Limeira Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~440 kt/yr fluff pulp (new line added ~2024, up from 100 kt); São Paulo state
operator: Suzano S.A.
source: Midland Paper / Suzano fluff pulp expansion announcement 2024; Suzano investor relations
notes: Limeira, São Paulo. Primarily fluff pulp (absorbent products). Smaller biogenic CO2 source than kraft mills. Recently expanded fluff capacity 4× (R$490M investment). No CCS plans.

name: Suzano Jacareí Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~600 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp; Jacareí, São Paulo state (older mill)
operator: Suzano S.A.
source: Suzano investor relations; Valmet and Suzano journey reference; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 600 kt
notes: Jacareí, São Paulo. Older mill with modest capacity compared to newer Suzano megaprojects. Located in Vale do Paraíba. No CCS plans. Proximity to São Paulo port may assist CO2 logistics if Brazil develops offshore storage.

name: Suzano Suzano-SP Pulp Mill (Original)
capacity_note: ~500 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp; the founding mill in Suzano municipality, São Paulo
operator: Suzano S.A.
source: Suzano company history; Environmental Paper Network; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 500 kt
notes: Suzano municipality, São Paulo. Company's original mill (founded 1924). Smaller, older facility in densely populated metro São Paulo region. Proximity to industry but limited CCS storage geology. No CCS plans.

name: Eldorado Brasil Três Lagoas Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 1,800 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp (exceeds nominal 1,500 kt/yr design); Três Lagoas, MS
operator: Eldorado Brasil Celulose S.A. (J&F group)
source: Andritz 'Complete pulp mill for Eldorado' reference; Eldorado Brasil website; Yokogawa case study 'World's Largest Single-line Pulp Mill'; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,800 kt
notes: Três Lagoas, Mato Grosso do Sul (BR-158, Km 231). One of the world's largest single-line eucalyptus pulp mills when commissioned 2012. Exceeded design capacity by 20%+. Sister mill to Suzano Três Lagoas complex. J&F group ownership (Friboi/JBS family). No CCS plans.

name: Klabin Monte Alegre / Telêmaco Borba Complex
capacity_note: ~1,700 kt/yr total combined (pulp + paperboard + paper); oldest Brazilian integrated pulp complex
operator: Klabin S.A.
source: Klabin Wikipedia; Klabin Our Units page; GEM Wiki Klabin power station; calc: ~0.82 t CO2/adt × 1,700 kt (mix of pulp types)
notes: Telêmaco Borba (Fazenda Monte Alegre), Paraná. Brazil's oldest integrated pulp mill, founded 1946. Multi-product: pine/eucalyptus pulp, paperboard, kraft paper. Includes a significant power station. No CCS plans. Klabin's largest site by output.

name: Klabin Otacílio Costa Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~400 kt/yr kraft pulp + packaging papers; Otacílio Costa, Santa Catarina
operator: Klabin S.A.
source: Klabin Wikipedia; Klabin Our Units page; BankTrack Klabin profile; calc: ~0.85 t CO2/adt × 400 kt
notes: Otacílio Costa, Santa Catarina. Integrated pulp and paper mill (packaging grades). Originally Igaras Papéis, acquired by Klabin 2000. No CCS plans. Smaller output relative to Klabin's Puma and Monte Alegre units.

name: Veracel Pulp Mill (Suzano / Stora Enso JV)
capacity_note: 1,100 kt/yr eucalyptus kraft pulp; Eunápolis, Bahia
operator: Veracel Celulose S.A. (Suzano 50% / Stora Enso 50% JV)
source: EIB Veracel project brief; IndustryAbout Veracel Eunápolis entry (coordinates -16.090508, -39.408465); Stora Enso Veracel location page; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,100 kt
notes: Eunápolis, southern Bahia. Owned 50% by Suzano and 50% by Stora Enso. Coastal Bahia location — relatively better CO2 transport potential. Stora Enso has active CCS programs in Scandinavia (Skutskär pilot) — potential to apply expertise here. No BECCS plans announced.

name: Bracell Lençóis Paulista Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~3,000 kt/yr kraft + dissolving pulp (post Project Star expansion, ~2022); Lençóis Paulista, SP
operator: Bracell SP Celulose Ltda (RGE group / Asia Pulp and Paper parent)
source: Bracell Project Star page; EUWID dissolving pulp start 2022; Bioenergy International Project Star rebranding; Papermart USD 996M tissue expansion; calc: ~0.83 t CO2/adt × 3,000 kt
notes: Lençóis Paulista, São Paulo. Post-Project Star expansion (~R$8B investment) makes this among Brazil's largest single-site pulp mills. Mix of dissolving pulp and kraft. Associated 109 MW power station from biomass. No CCS/BECCS plans. RGE/APP group. Brazil storage geology constrains BECCS.

name: Bracell Camaçari Pulp Mill (Bahia Specialty Cellulose)
capacity_note: ~500 kt/yr dissolving pulp; Complexo Industrial de Camaçari, Bahia
operator: Bracell (Bahia Specialty Cellulose / BSC; RGE group)
source: Bracell contact page (Rua Alfa 1033, Complexo Industrial de Camaçari); GEM Wiki Bahia Pulp power station (109 MW); Pulp and Paper Technology Bracell profile; calc: ~0.84 t CO2/adt × 500 kt
notes: Camaçari Industrial Complex, Bahia. Produces specialty dissolving pulp (viscose/textiles). Co-located 109 MW biomass power station. Part of Brazil's largest petrochemical/industrial cluster. No CCS plans. Coastal Bahia location is favorable for CO2 logistics if offshore storage developed.

name: CMPC Guaíba Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~2,400 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus (1,900 kt/yr + original 500 kt/yr line); Guaíba, Rio Grande do Sul
operator: CMPC Celulose Riograndense Ltda (CMPC S.A., Chile)
source: EUWID 'CMPC to raise Guaíba pulp mill capacity' Aug 2021; Valmet CMPC Guaíba odorless article; CMPC BioCMPC project page; Fastmarkets CMPC $4.6B new mill plan 2024
notes: Guaíba, Rio Grande do Sul (near Porto Alegre). Chile's CMPC second-largest Brazilian operation. Active sustainability program 'BioCMPC'. CMPC announced 2024 plans for new ~2,500 kt/yr mill in Brazil (separate greenfield). No BECCS plans for Guaíba but CMPC has global CCS interest.

name: Arauco MAPA Complex (Horcones), Chile
capacity_note: ~2,100 kt/yr total (1,560 kt/yr new MAPA eucalyptus line + 550 kt/yr modernized pine line); Arauco commune, Bío Bío
operator: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (ARAUCO; Empresas Copec subsidiary)
source: Valmet MAPA building the future article; ARAUCO MAPA ready to start operations (Empresas Copec 2022); Andritz MAPA eucalyptus article; ARAUCO Form 6-K SEC filing 2024
notes: Horcones, near Arauco city, Bío Bío region. MAPA project ($2.35B) added third pulp line (eucalyptus) and modernized existing pine line — now Chile's largest single pulp complex. Pacific coast location has CO2 transport potential. No CCS plans announced. Arauco is Chile's largest forestry company.

name: Arauco Nueva Aldea Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~1,100 kt/yr kraft pulp (856 kt/yr design, expanded post-start); Nueva Aldea, Ñuble region
operator: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (ARAUCO)
source: ResearchGate 'Arauco Nueva Aldea: The rocky road to higher capacity'; Fastmarkets restart after fire report; ARAUCO CDM biomass plant (Nueva Aldea Phase 2); calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,100 kt
notes: Nueva Aldea, Ñuble region (between Biobío and Maule). State-of-the-art single-line kraft mill, built ~2004. Adjacent biomass power plant (Phase 2 CDM project). Suffered major fire (plywood mill); pulp operations restarted. Moderate retrofit score — relatively new mill but Chile lacks CO2 storage infrastructure.

name: Arauco Valdivia Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~550 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus kraft pulp; San José de la Mariquina, Los Ríos region
operator: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (ARAUCO / CELCO)
source: Wikipedia Valdivia Pulp Mill (coordinates -39.5612878587, -72.8954104888); vymaps.com Planta Valdivia listing; Arauco mill catalog
notes: San José de la Mariquina, Los Ríos Region (built 2004). Co-generates 61 MW from volatiles/black liquor. Controversial for river pollution (Río Cruces wetland incident 2004–2005). Note: Licancel mill (154 kt/yr pine) was suspended indefinitely Sep 2023 due to floods/drought/fires — NOT included as viable retrofit target.

name: CMPC Santa Fe Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 1,469 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus kraft pulp; Nacimiento, Araucanía region
operator: CMPC Celulosa S.A. (CMPC group)
source: CMPC Pulp 'About Us' page; CMPC Pulp Santa Fe product page; CMPC Annual Report 2012; address: Av. Julio Hemmelmann 670, Nacimiento, Chile
notes: Nacimiento, Araucanía region, 600 km from Santiago. Largest white kraft cellulose plant in Chile. One of CMPC's most important pulp mills globally. No CCS plans. Chilean pulp industry has no active CCS/BECCS programs.

name: CMPC Pacífico Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~600 kt/yr BSKP radiata pine kraft pulp; Mininco, Biobío region
operator: CMPC Celulosa S.A. (CMPC group)
source: CMPC Pulp Pacífico page; address: Avda. Alessandri N°001, Mininco, Chile; CMPC Pulp About Us page
notes: Mininco, Biobío region. Radiata pine softwood pulp. Part of CMPC's three-mill Chile cluster (Santa Fe + Pacífico + Laja). CMPC Laja (293 kt/yr, oldest mill ~1958) also in region but smaller — not separately listed.

name: Montes del Plata Pulp Mill (Punta Pereira)
capacity_note: 1,300 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus kraft pulp; Punta Pereira (Conchillas), Colonia dept.
operator: Montes del Plata S.A. (Arauco 50% / Stora Enso 50% JV)
source: Stora Enso 'Montes del Plata Mill' location page; ANDRITZ Montes del Plata reference; Montes del Plata company page; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,300 kt
notes: Punta Pereira, near Conchillas, Colonia department (Ruta 55). Rio de la Plata estuary location — potential for future CO2 transport/export. Opened 2014; JV between Arauco and Stora Enso. Uruguay lacks CO2 storage geology but coastal location offers modest advantage. No CCS plans.

name: UPM Fray Bentos Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 1,300 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus kraft pulp (expanded from 1,100 kt/yr); Fray Bentos, Río Negro dept.
operator: UPM Fray Bentos (UPM-Kymmene; 100% since 2009)
source: UPM Pulp Fray Bentos page; ForestIndustries.EU UPM Fray Bentos article; Andritz UPM Uruguay article; Ruta Vladimir Roslik Km. 307, 65000 Fray Bentos; calc: ~0.87 t CO2/adt × 1,300 kt
notes: Fray Bentos, Río Negro department, Uruguay (Uruguay River banks). Operational since 2007. UPM's second mill in Uruguay (alongside Paso de los Toros). Combined UPM Uruguay capacity now ~3.4 Mt/yr eucalyptus pulp. No BECCS plans. Uruguay storage geology absent.

name: Sappi Ngodwana Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~340 kt/yr chemical pulp + 255 kt/yr DWP + 350 kt/yr paper (newsprint/kraft); Ngodwana, Mpumalanga
operator: Sappi Southern Africa Ltd (Sappi Limited)
source: Sappi Ngodwana Mill page; GeoView ZA Sappi Ngodwana (MapCarta W95805200); Sappi Global Africa Network 2024 article; Sappi Annual Reports
notes: Elands Valley, ~50 km from Mbombela (Nelspruit), Mpumalanga. Integrated pulp and paper mill. Produces kraft pulp, DWP (dissolving wood pulp), and paper grades. South Africa's primary pulp producing region. Sappi is a major kraft pulp exporter. No BECCS/CCS plans but Sappi has global sustainability ambitions.

name: Sappi Saiccor Dissolving Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~1,500 kt/yr acid sulphide dissolving wood pulp (DWP); world's largest DWP mill; Umkomaas, KZN
operator: Sappi Southern Africa Ltd (Sappi Limited)
source: Sappi Saiccor Mill page ('1.5 million ton capacity, 15% global DP market share'); Sappi in South Africa TAPPI report; Umkomanzi Drift, Umkomaas 4170
notes: Umkomaas, 50 km south of Durban, KwaZulu-Natal. World's largest dissolving wood pulp (DWP) mill — acid sulphite process rather than kraft. Strong coastal position (Indian Ocean coast). Sappi Saiccor has environmental compliance history. South Africa has no CO2 storage infrastructure. Moderate retrofit score — world-scale plant with coastal CO2 transport potential.

name: Sappi Tugela Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~200 kt/yr NSSC pulp + corrugating medium papers; Mandeni, KZN north coast
operator: Sappi Southern Africa Ltd
source: Sappi Tugela Mill page; KZN Top Business directory; Old Main Road, Mandeni 4490
notes: Mandeni, KwaZulu-Natal north coast (near Tugela River). Neutral sulphite semi-chemical (NSSC) pulp — not kraft. Produces corrugating medium for packaging. Smaller biogenic CO2 source. Low retrofit score due to process type and South Africa's absent CCS infrastructure.

name: Mondi Richards Bay Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~720 kt/yr total (Baycel bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp + Baywhite white-top linerboard); Richards Bay, KZN
operator: Mondi South Africa (Pty) Ltd (Mondi plc; after Syktyvkar Russia exit, African ops retained)
source: Mondi Richards Bay location page; Mondi Facebook operational highlight (720 kt/yr post-expansion); GEM Wiki Richards Bay Mill power station; 7 Western Arterial, Richards Bay 3900
notes: Richards Bay, KwaZulu-Natal. Deep-water port location — Richards Bay is South Africa's largest bulk export terminal. Produces Baycel (kraft pulp) and Baywhite (linerboard). CO2 transport via ship is plausible here if South African offshore storage is developed. Mondi sold Russian Syktyvkar mill 2023 (governance risk). Richards Bay retained.

name: Ilim Bratsk Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~720 kt/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp (one of world's largest fiberlines after modernization); Bratsk, Irkutsk Oblast
operator: Ilim Group (International Paper exited 2022; now Russian-controlled)
source: Ilim Group website Bratsk branch; Lesprom 'Ilim inaugurates world's largest fiberline in Bratsk'; SST Group Ilim project; Bratsk coordinates from geodatos.net: 56.1325, 101.61417
notes: Bratsk, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia. One of world's largest softwood pulp fiberlines after modernization. Ilim Group is Russia's largest pulp & paper company. International Paper exited 2022 (Russia sanctions/ESG). Low retrofit score: Russia's isolated Siberian location, geopolitical risk, lack of CCS infrastructure and policy under current government, and sanctions limiting Western technology transfer.

name: Ilim Ust-Ilimsk Pulp & Cardboard Complex
capacity_note: ~1,500 kt/yr at full capacity (pulp + new 600 kt/yr cardboard mill commissioned 2024); Ust-Ilimsk, Irkutsk Oblast
operator: Ilim Group
source: Interfax 'Ilim Group to bring Ust-Ilimsk up to design capacity in 2025'; Ilim Group Ust-Ilimsk Big Project press release; Ilim Group website; tadviser.com Ilim financial profile
notes: Ust-Ilimsk, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia. Major expansion: new 600 kt/yr bleached packaging cardboard mill (100 billion rubles investment) received operational permission Feb 2024. Total site ~1,500 kt/yr at full capacity. Very low retrofit score: all constraints of Bratsk apply plus even more remote location.

name: Ilim Koryazhma Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~1,200 kt/yr total annual output (one of Europe's largest chemical pulp & paper mills); Koryazhma, Arkhangelsk Oblast
operator: Ilim Group (formerly Kotlas Pulp and Paper Mill)
source: Ilim Group Koryazhma branch page; Wikipedia Koryazhma (61.30°N, 47.16°E — on Vychegda River, 30 km east of Kotlas); ANDRITZ Koryazhma wood processing 2019 announcement; Ilim Group overall capacity data
notes: Koryazhma, Arkhangelsk Oblast, northwest Russia (Vychegda River). Formerly Kotlas PPM — one of USSR's showcase facilities. Produces pulp, paper, and cardboard. Geopolitically higher risk than Siberian mills given proximity to NATO/Baltic access routes. No CCS.

name: Arkhangelsk Pulp & Paper Mill (Novodvinsk)
capacity_note: ~1,000 kt/yr+ total (cardboard KDM-4 line ~400 kt/yr added 2024; oldest major Russian PPM)
operator: AO Arkhangelsk PPM (formerly partly International Paper; now Russian state/private)
source: Pulp & Paper Technology supplier profile; PulpPaperNews KDM-4 cardboard machine 2024; Barents Observer 'Russia's first new PPM in 40 years'
notes: Novodvinsk, Arkhangelsk Oblast, northwest Russia (near Arkhangelsk port). Adding KDM-4 cardboard machine (400 kt/yr), expected 2024 commissioning. Northern Russian location with White Sea access. All Russia geopolitical/governance concerns apply. Low retrofit score.

name: Mondi Syktyvkar (now Sezar Group)
capacity_note: ~1,200 kt/yr integrated pulp + containerboard + fine paper; Syktyvkar, Komi Republic
operator: Sezar Group (acquired from Mondi plc 2022–2023 at ~80 bln rubles; post-Russia-exit)
source: EUWID 'Mondi divestment of Syktyvkar completed'; Mondi announcement EUR 1.5B sale; Andritz Mondi Syktyvkar Spectrum article; Packaging Gateway Syktyvkar project profile
notes: Syktyvkar, Komi Republic. Former Mondi flagship — 1,200 kt/yr integrated facility. Mondi sold following Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion (ESG/sanctions pressure). Now Sezar Group. Very low retrofit score: loss of Western operator expertise, Russia governance/geopolitical risk, sanctions, no CCS policy. Included for scale completeness.

name: Segezha Group Segezha Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~384 kt/yr sack kraft paper (primary product); Segezha town, Republic of Karelia
operator: Segezha Group PJSC (AFK Sistema, majority shareholder)
source: ABB Segezha project reference; Segezha Group website; PulpPaperNews Segezha Sokol paper machine article; Papnews Big Ust-Ilimsk project
notes: Segezha, Republic of Karelia (700 km north of St Petersburg). Segezha Group is Russia's second-largest forestry/paper company. Primarily sack kraft paper. Segezha also operates Sokol PPM in Vologda Oblast. Low retrofit score: Russia geopolitical/governance concerns, no CCS policy.

name: ISTAÇ Odayeri Waste-to-Energy Plant, Istanbul
capacity_note: ~85 MW electrical / 175 MWh thermal; 3,000 t/day / ~1.1 Mt/yr MSW; Turkey's first WtE, Europe's largest
operator: İstanbul Environmental Management Co. (İSTAÇ), a subsidiary of Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality; operated by Veolia since ~2023
source: Wikipedia Istanbul Waste Power Plant (coords 41°13′30″N 28°48′54″E = 41.225, 28.815); AIIB project page; Veolia press release Apr 2023; Balkan Green Energy News Istanbul WtE expansion
notes: Eyüp district, Istanbul (Kısırmandıra area, near Odayeri landfill). Operational since Nov 2021. Built by Hitachi Zosen Inova / Makyol consortium. AIIB funded. Veolia became operator 2023. Claimed 'Europe's largest WtE' by some sources (by AIIB investment). Turkey has no CO2 storage infrastructure and limited CCS policy — low retrofit score. Turkish MSW biogenic fraction ~45–55%. Biogenic CO2 ~0.35 Mt/yr (50% of ~0.7 Mt total CO2).

name: Raízen Araraquara Bioenergy Complex (Barra Grande)
capacity_note: ~7.5 Mt cane/yr; one of Raízen's largest single-unit complexes, São Paulo
operator: Raízen S.A. (bp 100% since 2024; formerly Shell/Cosan JV)
source: Raízen Wikipedia; bp completes Bunge Bioenergia acquisition Bioenergy Insight; Raízen investor relations; calc: ~81 kg CO2/t cane × 7.5 Mt cane = 0.61 Mt CO2
notes: Araraquara region, São Paulo. One of Raízen's large São Paulo state complexes. bp acquired 100% of Bunge Bioenergia JV assets 2024, giving bp 23 mills across Brazil. Raízen separately still has ~23 mills. Sugarcane ethanol fermentation CO2 is pure stream — ideal for low-cost capture. Not excluded by Frontier (sugarcane). No CCS announced.

name: BP Bioenergia Pedro Afonso Bioenergy Complex
capacity_note: ~7 Mt cane/yr; largest single unit in bp Bioenergia portfolio; Tocantins state; R$530M expansion 2024
operator: bp Bunge Bioenergia / bp Bioenergia (bp 100% since Q4 2024)
source: Global Flow Control 'BP Bunge announces expansion of R$530 million Pedro Afonso' press release; bp Form 6-K SEC filing 2024; Bunge Form 8-K 2024 sale announcement
notes: Pedro Afonso, Tocantins. Northernmost of bp's Brazilian mills. R$530M expansion announced 2024. Part of bp's 11-mill Brazil bioenergy portfolio (32 Mt/yr combined crushing). Tocantins state has very limited CO2 storage options. Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. bp's global CCS expertise (bp owns North Sea CCS assets) could theoretically be deployed here but Brazil logistics make this low priority.

name: Jalles Machado / Otávio Lage Bioenergy Complex
capacity_note: ~9 Mt sugarcane/yr combined (two mills); 142 MW installed cogeneration; Goianésia, Goiás
operator: Jalles Machado S.A. (Goianésia, Goiás; listed on B3)
source: Jalles website (Goianésia, Goiás); IFC Jalles project page 49275; Jalles RI performance sectors page; calc: ~81 kg CO2/t cane × 9 Mt = 0.73 Mt CO2
notes: Goianésia, Goiás. Two mills (Jalles Machado + Otávio Lage) with combined 9 Mt/yr crushing, 142 MW cogeneration (64% surplus to grid). IFC invested in biogas project (R$94M, 2024). Active sustainability development — biogas from vinasse is in progress. Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. No CCS plans.

name: Tereos Brasil Ipaussu Bioenergy Complex
capacity_note: ~5.5 Mt cane/yr (Ipaussu unit, one of Tereos Brazil's 7 plants); São Paulo state
operator: Tereos Group (French cooperative; 7 Brazil mills total)
source: Tereos Group Brazil operations; Hydrocarbon Processing 'Brazil mills boost sugar capacity' Mar 2024; calc: ~81 kg CO2/t cane × 5.5 Mt = 0.45 Mt CO2
notes: Ipaussu, São Paulo state. Tereos is France's largest sugar group, with 7 plants in Brazil (~30 Mt/yr combined crushing across portfolio). Prioritizes sugar over ethanol in 2024 flex. Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. European Tereos parent has some CCS awareness but no Brazil CCS plans. Moderate retrofit score for São Paulo location near industry.

name: Ledesma Ingenio Sugar/Ethanol Mill
capacity_note: ~40,000 ha sugarcane; 51 MW bioelectricity; bioethanol plant (~100 ML/yr); Libertador G.S.M., Jujuy
operator: Ledesma S.A.A.I. (Blaquier family)
source: Wikipedia Ledesma S.A.A.I.; Sugaronline ethanol expansion 2017; Encyclopedia.com Ledesma company history; Wikimapia Ingenio Ledesma coords (23°49'38"S, 64°47'20"W = -23.83, -64.79)
notes: Libertador General San Martín, Jujuy province (Andean foothills, NW Argentina). Diversified operations: sugarcane, sugar, ethanol, paper, cellulose. 51 MW bagasse cogeneration. Argentina has no CCS infrastructure and limited storage geology in Jujuy region. Ledesma also operates forestry/paper division. Low retrofit score: governance/regulatory context, lack of infrastructure.

name: Tabacal / Seaboard Ingenio Sugar Mill
capacity_note: ~30 MW bagasse cogeneration; sugar + ethanol; Hipólito Yrigoyen, Salta province
operator: Seaboard Energías Renovables y Alimentos S.R.L. (Seaboard Corp, USA)
source: GEM Wiki Ingenio Tabacal power station; Seaboard Corp Tabacal company page; location: Hipólito Yrigoyen, ~25 km from Orán, Salta
notes: Hipólito Yrigoyen (El Tabacal), Salta, Argentina (~23.2°S, 64.3°W est. from proximity to Orán). Sugar, ethanol, and 30 MW cogeneration from bagasse. Seaboard Corp US-owned. Remote Andean foothills location. No CCS. Lower priority than Ledesma due to smaller scale.

name: Incauca Sugar Mill & Bioethanol Plant
capacity_note: 70 MW cogeneration (33 MWh avg, 10 MWh to grid); sugarcane bioethanol; El Ortigal, Cauca dept.
operator: Ingenio del Cauca S.A.S. (Incauca; Cauca Valley sugar group)
source: Incauca location page (El Ortigal, 50 km from Cali, 134 km from Popayán); Incauca history page; Sugar mills in Colombia overview; WEG solutions Colombia article
notes: El Ortigal, Cauca Department, Colombia (50 km from Cali). Colombia's largest sugar mill. 70 MW cogeneration from bagasse. Sugarcane ethanol (not corn — not excluded by Frontier). Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. Colombia has no CO2 storage infrastructure and limited CCS policy. Low retrofit score but notable as largest Colombian sugar facility.

name: Manuelita Sugar & Bioethanol Mill
capacity_note: ~4.2 Mt cane/yr; integrated sugar, ethanol, biofuels; Palmira, Valle del Cauca
operator: Manuelita S.A. (Eder family; founded 1864)
source: Wikipedia Manuelita (4.2 Mt cane/yr; Palmira, Valle del Cauca); Colombia One 'Colombia Turns Sugarcane Waste Into Power' Feb 2026; Sugaronline Manuelita cogeneration Brazil investment
notes: Palmira, Valle del Cauca (Colombia's sugar valley, Cauca River valley). Colombia's oldest sugar mill (1864). 4.2 Mt/yr processing — largest single site in Colombia by crushing. Manuelita also has operations in Peru (Arena Dulce). Cogeneration from bagasse. No CCS plans in Colombia.

name: Tongaat Hulett Felixton Sugar Mill (KZN Biomass Cogen)
capacity_note: 31.5 MWe bagasse cogeneration; ~2.5 Mt sugarcane/yr crushing capacity; Empangeni, KZN
operator: Tongaat Hulett Sugar (now under new ownership after Tongaat Hulett restructuring 2022–2023)
source: Power Technology Felixton Sugar Cogeneration Plant profile (31.5 MW); vymaps.com Felixton Mill coords (-28.83582, 31.89243); Tongaat Hulett South Africa page; ScienceDirect LCA bagasse cogeneration South Africa
notes: Felixton, Empangeni area, KZN north coast (~160 km north of Durban). Part of Tongaat Hulett's three KZN mills (Felixton, Maidstone, Amatikulu). Combined annual cogeneration: ~436,000 MWh from bagasse. Tongaat Hulett underwent major restructuring/receivership 2022–2023. South Africa has no CO2 storage infrastructure. Low retrofit score. Note: CO2 from bagasse combustion (not fermentation) — mixed-source flue gas, more complex capture.

name: Illovo Sugar Merebank Distillery / KZN Cogen Cluster
capacity_note: ~20–30 MWe bagasse cogeneration (Merebank + south Durban distillery complex); KwaZulu-Natal
operator: Illovo Sugar Africa (Associated British Foods group)
source: South Africa Sugar Manufacturing Market Report 2020 (BusinessWire); ScienceDirect LCA cogeneration South African sugar; Illovo Sugar corporate website
notes: Illovo Sugar Africa is the African continent's largest sugar producer (7 countries). KZN operations include Merebank distillery and sugar processing with bagasse cogeneration. Illovo's combined SA bagasse energy output is modest vs Tongaat Hulett. No CCS plans. ABF parent has global sustainability commitments but no CCS roadmap for African sugar operations.

name: Arauco Nueva Aldea Biomass Power Plant
capacity_note: ~48 MWe biomass (bark/wood residues, separate from pulp mill recovery boiler); Nueva Aldea, Chile
operator: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (ARAUCO)
source: Nueva Aldea Biomass Power Plant Phase 2 CDM project document (fokus-zukunft.com / UNFCCC CDM registry); Arauco operations
notes: Dedicated biomass power plant (Phase 2) adjacent to Nueva Aldea pulp mill. Registered as CDM project. Burns bark, wood chips, and forest residues. Separate from the pulp mill's recovery boiler. Chile has no CO2 storage policy or infrastructure — low retrofit score despite being capturable biogenic CO2 source.

name: Rybinsk / Cherepovets Biomass CHP (Vologda Oblast)
capacity_note: ~100 MWth biomass CHP district heating (wood residues, bark); Cherepovets, Vologda Oblast
operator: Various municipal/industrial operators (Severstal-affiliated or municipal energy); representative of Russian regional biomass CHP sector
source: IEA Bioenergy Russia country report; Russian biomass energy sector overview; calc: 100 MWth at 8,000 hrs/yr × 0.35 tCO2/MWh biogenic
notes: Representative facility for Russia's wood-waste biomass CHP sector in the European north. Vologda / Cherepovets region is one of Russia's largest wood-processing areas. Severstal's forestry operations generate substantial wood residues. Many small-medium biomass CHP plants operate in this region for district heating. No CCS policy in Russia's biomass energy sector. Low retrofit score.

name: URE Barueri Waste-to-Energy Plant (Orizon)
capacity_note: ~20 MW; 825 t/day (~300 kt/yr MSW); first Latin American mass-burn WtE; Barueri, São Paulo metro
operator: Orizon Valorização de Resíduos S.A. (SENER engineering)
source: SENER press release 'First Latin American waste energy recovery plant'; WasteCulture legal aspects URE Barueri case study; BNamericas Barueri thermoelectric plant profile; operations expected ~2027
notes: Barueri, São Paulo metropolitan area (~26.5 km from São Paulo center). First mass-burn WtE plant in Latin America under construction (designed by SENER for Orizon). Operations expected ~2027. 300 kt/yr MSW throughput, 20 MW. Brazil MSW is biogenic-rich (~60%). Biogenic CO2 est: ~0.08 Mt/yr (50% of total ~0.16 Mt). Too small for commercial CCS. Important as Brazil's inaugural WtE BECCS candidate.

name: Arauco Sucuruí Pulp Mill, Mato Grosso do Sul (planned)
capacity_note: ~3,500 kt/yr BHKP eucalyptus (greenfield; $5.5B investment announced 2024); Água Clara, MS
operator: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (ARAUCO)
source: ARAUCO Sucuruí Project PDF (Conference Call, Sep 2024); ARAUCO Form 6-K SEC filing 2024; Bioenergy International Arauco MAPA approval
notes: Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul (Três Lagoas region). Greenfield announced 2024 — would be world's largest single pulp production line (~3,500 kt/yr, ~$5.5B). Would surpass Suzano Cerrado (2,550 kt/yr). Target start: 2028–2030. Brazilian storage geology constrains BECCS. Included as future high-priority BECCS candidate. CO2 estimate is forward-looking at full capacity.
